newsitem.title: SPAIN: Pryca shares fall on poor 9-month sales.
newsitem.headline: Pryca shares fall on poor 9-month sales.

text.p: Shares in Spanish hypermarket Pryca were down sharply in midmorning trade on Thursday after news that gross sales fell 0.3 percent in the nine months to September, traders and analysts said.
At 0930 GMT shares in Pryca were down 60 pesetas, or 1.93 percent, to 3,050. The Ibex-35 index was down 6.47 points, 0.15 percent to 4,255.92.

"Pryca still expect profits to rise 10-15 percent by the end of the year, which I think may be optimistic. They're confident that October and November sales will be positive. But still they've been much more cautious about the second half of the year. I think the shares may be a little overvalued," said an analyst who requested anonymity.
She said that taking into effect calendar changes, sales in September alone fell around seven percent.

"I have a neutral opinion on Pryca at the moment, but it's sure that sales are not very good. (French majority stake owner) Carrefour were a little disappointed that these figures were worse than they expected. They don't know why, they just know that things are difficult in Spain," she added.
However she added that good cost management and relatively stable margins had helped to offset weaker sales.
She set a fair value target for Pryca at around 3,000 pesetas.
